Script.name: 00_util
Script.script:
--[[ aardkit core utils Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31 Shared helpers for the ported MUSHclient plugins. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.version = "1.0.0"
local U = {} aardkit.util = U
--- -- paths ---
-- everything we persist lives under <profile>/aardkit/ function U.datadir() local d = getMudletHomeDir() .. "/aardkit" if not io.exists(d) then lfs.mkdir(d) end return d end
function U.datafile(name) return U.datadir() .. "/" .. name end
--- -- persistence — one table per key, saved as a Lua chunk ---
function U.save(key, tbl) local ok, err = pcall(table.save, U.datafile(key .. ".lua"), tbl) if not ok then aardkit.util.err("save " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end return ok end
-- Defaults are a floor, not a fallback: whatever loads gets laid over them, so a -- truncated or half-written state file costs you the saved values, not the keys. -- Without this a bad file returns an empty table and the first plugin that does -- arithmetic on a config field dies at load time and takes itself out. function U.load(key, default) local out = {} for k, v in pairs(default or {}) do out[k] = v end
local path = U.datafile(key .. ".lua") if not io.exists(path) then return out end
local t = {} if not pcall(table.load, path, t) then U.warn("couldn't read " .. key .. ".lua - using defaults") return out end for k, v in pairs(t) do out[k] = v end return out end
--- -- output -- -- Everything we print uses <#rrggbb> tags, which is NOT a syntax any Mudlet echo -- accepts: cecho wants colour *names*, hecho wants #rrggbb, decho wants <r,g,b>. -- Feed cecho a <#rrggbb> and it quietly drops it, which is how the whole thing -- came out plain. So convert to decho: it's bracket-delimited, so a '#' or a -- comma sitting in the message text can't be mistaken for markup the way it can -- with hecho. ---
local function to_decho(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("<#(%x%x%x%x%x%x)>", function(h) return string.format("<%d,%d,%d>", tonumber(h:sub(1, 2), 16), tonumber(h:sub(3, 4), 16), tonumber(h:sub(5, 6), 16)) end)) end
U.to_decho = to_decho
-- main window function U.out(s) decho(to_decho(s)) end
-- a named console / miniwindow function U.outw(win, s) decho(win, to_decho(s)) end
--- -- compat -- -- Mudlet's C++ API is greppable in the binary; its Lua-side API (Geyser, db, -- LuaGlobal) is compressed into a Qt resource and is not. So anything below that -- lives on the Lua side gets checked at runtime instead of assumed — guessing -- wrong there is how 'clearMap' shipped as a nil call. ---
function U.has(name) return type(_G[name]) == "function" end
--- -- links -- -- dechoLink is the right one: it takes <r,g,b>, which is what to_decho already -- produces. cechoLink was tried and is wrong - it only knows colour names, so -- our <#3ad07a> printed literally. -- -- What was actually broken is the command. Mudlet's own code passes a function -- (mudlet-lua/GUIUtils.lua, cechoLink -> xEcho -> echoLink), and a function is -- unambiguous where a string is Lua to be eval'd at click time, with the -- quoting left to every call site - a mob called Doctor Cameroon "Rusty" Baboon -- is the sort of thing that goes wrong there. Strings still work, they get -- wrapped. -- -- The trailing boolean is useCurrentFormat and xEcho does accept it: four args -- with a boolean fourth is the documented no-window form. ---
local function asfunc(cmd) if type(cmd) == "function" then return cmd end local s = tostring(cmd or "") local compile = loadstring or load return function() local fn = compile(s) if fn then fn() end end end
local function plain(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("<[^>]*>", "")) end
function U.outLink(s, cmd, hint) local fn = asfunc(cmd) if U.has("dechoLink") and pcall(dechoLink, to_decho(s), fn, hint or "", true) then return end if U.has("echoLink") then echoLink(plain(s), fn, hint or "", true) return end U.out(s) end
function U.outLinkw(win, s, cmd, hint) local fn = asfunc(cmd) if U.has("dechoLink") and pcall(dechoLink, win, to_decho(s), fn, hint or "", true) then return end if U.has("echoLink") then echoLink(win, plain(s), fn, hint or "", true) return end U.outw(win, s) end
function U.killhandler(id) if id and U.has("killAnonymousEventHandler") then pcall(killAnonymousEventHandler, id) end end
-- Repeating timer built on tempTimer, which is C++ and definitely there. -- registerNamedTimer would do this too, but it's Lua-side and unverifiable, and -- a self-rearming tempTimer keyed on a generation counter is no more code. U.timers = U.timers or {}
function U.every(key, secs, fn) U.timers[key] = (U.timers[key] or 0) + 1 local gen = U.timers[key] local function tick() if U.timers[key] ~= gen then return end -- superseded or cancelled local ok, err = pcall(fn) if not ok then U.err("timer " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end if U.timers[key] == gen then tempTimer(secs, tick) end end tempTimer(secs, tick) end
function U.unevery(key) U.timers[key] = (U.timers[key] or 0) + 1 -- orphans any tick in flight end
local TAG = "<#7aa2f7>[<#e94560>aardkit<#7aa2f7>]<r> "
function U.note(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#c8d0dc>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
function U.ok(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#9ece6a>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
function U.warn(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#e0af68>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
function U.err(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#f7768e>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
-- help blocks: pass a list of {cmd, description} and it lines them up function U.help(title, rows) U.out("\n<#7aa2f7>" .. title .. "<r>") local w = 0 for _, r in ipairs(rows) do w = math.max(w, #r[1]) end for _, r in ipairs(rows) do if r[2] then U.out("\n <#e0af68>" .. r[1] .. string.rep(" ", w - #r[1]) .. "<r> <#c8d0dc>" .. r[2] .. "<r>") else U.out("\n <#8a93a8>" .. r[1] .. "<r>") end end echo("\n") end
--- -- strings ---
function U.trim(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")) end
-- "buffer 200" -> "buffer", "200" function U.split_verb(s) s = U.trim(s) local verb, rest = s:match("^(%S+)%s*(.*)$") return (verb or ""):lower(), rest or "" end
-- db: stores numeric columns as REAL, so a room id reads back 16298.0 function U.rid(n) return string.format("%d", math.floor(tonumber(n) or 0)) end
function U.commas(n) local s = tostring(math.floor(tonumber(n) or 0)) local out = s:reverse():gsub("(%d%d%d)", "%1,"):reverse() return (out:gsub("^,", "")) end
-- 4211 -> "1h 10m", for last-seen columns function U.duration(secs) secs = math.floor(tonumber(secs) or 0) if secs < 60 then return secs .. "s" end local m = math.floor(secs / 60) if m < 60 then return m .. "m" end local h = math.floor(m / 60) if h < 24 then return h .. "h " .. (m % 60) .. "m" end return math.floor(h / 24) .. "d " .. (h % 24) .. "h" end
-- Aardwolf sends colour codes as @x123 / @R etc in some channels; strip for storage function U.strip_codes(s) s = tostring(s or "") s = s:gsub("@x%d%d?%d?", ""):gsub("@[%a@]", "") return s end
-- Aardwolf @ codes -> hex, for rendering a stored/echoed @-coded string locally local ACOLOR = { r = "#800000", R = "#ff0000", g = "#008000", G = "#00ff00", y = "#808000", Y = "#ffff00", b = "#000080", B = "#0000ff", m = "#800080", M = "#ff00ff", c = "#008080", C = "#00ffff", w = "#c0c0c0", W = "#ffffff", D = "#808080", }
-- xterm 256 -> hex, the standard cube + greyscale ramp local function xterm(n) n = tonumber(n) or 0 if n < 16 then local basic = { "#000000", "#800000", "#008000", "#808000", "#000080", "#800080", "#008080", "#c0c0c0", "#808080", "#ff0000", "#00ff00", "#ffff00", "#0000ff", "#ff00ff", "#00ffff", "#ffffff" } return basic[n + 1] or "#c0c0c0" end if n < 232 then local i = n - 16 local lv = { 0, 95, 135, 175, 215, 255 } return string.format("#%02x%02x%02x", lv[math.floor(i / 36) % 6 + 1], lv[math.floor(i / 6) % 6 + 1], lv[i % 6 + 1]) end local g = 8 + (n - 232) * 10 return string.format("#%02x%02x%02x", g, g, g) end
-- turn an @-coded string into something cecho understands. $C is a server-side -- channel reset the codes don't cover, so locally it just reads as white. function U.acolor(s) s = tostring(s or ""):gsub("%$C", "@w") s = s:gsub("@x(%d%d?%d?)", function(n) return "<" .. xterm(n) .. ">" end) s = s:gsub("@(%a)", function(c) return ACOLOR[c] and ("<" .. ACOLOR[c] .. ">") or "" end) return (s:gsub("@@", "@")) end
function U.aecho(s) U.out("\n" .. U.acolor(s) .. "<r>") end
--- -- gmcp ---
-- current room vnum, or nil if gmcp hasn't landed yet function U.room() local r = gmcp and gmcp.room and gmcp.room.info if not r then return nil end return tonumber(r.num), r.name, r.zone end
function U.charname() local c = gmcp and gmcp.char and gmcp.char.base and gmcp.char.base.name return c or getProfileName() end
-- Aardwolf sets char.status.state; 3 = playing function U.playing() local st = gmcp and gmcp.char and gmcp.char.status and gmcp.char.status.state return tonumber(st) == 3 end

Script.name: 10_panel
Script.script:
--[[ aardkit panel manager Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
Every ported plugin that used to draw a MUSHclient miniwindow gets one of these instead. Two modes:
embed - Adjustable.Container inside the main window. Drag the title bar, drag the edges to resize, right-click for the built-in menu. The container saves and reloads its own geometry. dock - Geyser.UserWindow, a real Qt dock widget. Drag it out to float, drag it back to dock it to any edge. Mudlet stores that layout in windowLayout.dat by itself.
Which mode each panel is in (and whether it's hidden) is ours to remember, so a panel comes back the way you left it. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.panel = aardkit.panel or {}
local P = aardkit.panel local U = aardkit.util
P.reg = P.reg or {} -- name -> panel P.state = P.state or {} -- name -> {mode=, hidden=}
local DEFAULT_MODE = "embed"
-- Doubles as the title bar height: Adjustable.Container places contents at -- padding*2. Mudlet's own default is 10; the close/minimise buttons are 15px -- tall sitting at y=4, so anything under 10 clips them and the title too. local TITLEBAR = 10
local STYLE = { bg = "#0d1117", bar = "#161b2e", border = "#3a4a6b", title = "#e94560", text = "#c8d0dc", }
local function container_style() return [[ background-color: rgba(13,17,23,235); border: 1px solid ]] .. STYLE.border .. [[; border-radius: 3px; ]] end
--- -- state ---
local function load_state() P.state = U.load("panels", {}) end
local function save_state() U.save("panels", P.state) end
local function st(name) P.state[name] = P.state[name] or {} return P.state[name] end
--- -- buffer migration — carry the scrollback (with its colours) across a mode flip ---
local function migrate(from, to) if not from or not to then return end local n = getLineCount(from) if not n or n < 1 then return end local first = math.max(1, n - 500) -- 500 lines is plenty to carry over for i = first, n - 1 do moveCursor(from, 0, i) selectCurrentLine(from) copy(from) appendBuffer(to) end moveCursorEnd(from) end
--- -- panel ---
local Panel = {} Panel.__index = Panel
function Panel:_build() local s = st(self.name) local mode = s.mode or self.defmode
-- bumped every rebuild so widget names stay unique; Mudlet keeps the old -- label objects alive and reusing a name orphans them self.gen = (self.gen or 0) + 1
if mode == "dock" then self.holder = Geyser.UserWindow:new({ name = self.name .. "_uw" .. self.gen, titleText = self.title, }) else self.holder = Adjustable.Container:new({ name = self.name .. "_ac" .. self.gen, x = self.x, y = self.y, width = self.w, height = self.h, titleText = self.title, titleTxtColor = STYLE.title, adjLabelstyle = container_style(), padding = TITLEBAR, autoSave = true, autoLoad = true, })
-- Adjustable.Container puts its contents at y = padding*2 and draws the -- title above that, so padding IS the title bar height. At 4 that left -- 8px for a 12px title and the console covered it. Worse, padding is -- saved with the geometry and restored on load, so the constructor value -- above gets overwritten by whatever the file remembers - it has to be -- set again afterwards or old saves keep the cramped bar forever. if self.holder.setPadding then pcall(function() self.holder:setPadding(TITLEBAR) end) end end
self.mode = mode
-- Measure and parent against the CONTENT box, not the outer frame. An -- Adjustable.Container's Inside starts at x=padding, so anything that sized -- itself off the outer width then drew from that offset origin overhung the -- right edge by exactly padding - which is why the recall buttons ran past -- the border, and why raising padding to 10 made it worse. self.container = type(self.holder.Inside) == "table" and self.holder.Inside or self.holder
if not self.consoleless then local old = self.console and self.console.name self.console = Geyser.MiniConsole:new({ name = self.name .. "_con" .. self.gen, x = 0, y = 0, width = "100%", height = "100%", autoWrap = self.wrap ~= false, color = STYLE.bg, fontSize = self.fontSize or 9, scrollBar = true, }, self.holder) self.console:setColor(STYLE.bg) if old then migrate(old, self.console.name) end end
if self.onbuild then local ok, err = pcall(self.onbuild, self) if not ok then U.err("panel " .. self.name .. " onbuild: " .. tostring(err)) end end end
function Panel:show() self.holder:show() self:raise() st(self.name).hidden = false save_state() end
function Panel:hide() self.holder:hide() st(self.name).hidden = true save_state() end
function Panel:visible() return not st(self.name).hidden end
function Panel:toggle() if self:visible() then self:hide() else self:show() end end
function Panel:setmode(mode) if mode ~= "dock" and mode ~= "embed" then U.warn("panel mode must be dock or embed") return end if mode == self.mode then return end
local oldholder, oldcon = self.holder, self.console st(self.name).mode = mode self:_build()
-- the new console pulled the scrollback across in _build; drop the old shell if oldcon then oldcon:hide() end if oldholder then oldholder:hide() end
if self:visible() then self:show() else self:hide() end save_state() U.ok(self.name .. " -> " .. mode) end
-- The AardwolfMudlet GUI frame builds after us and lands on top, which is how a -- panel gets "lost" under the chat tabs. -- -- raiseWindow() needs a REAL widget name. A Geyser container isn't one - only -- the labels and consoles inside it are actual Mudlet windows - so raising the -- container by name silently does nothing. -- -- Order matters and it bit us: raiseWindow puts a widget on TOP, so whoever is -- raised last wins. Walking windowList with pairs() is a random order, so some -- runs raised the container's own backdrop last and painted it over the panel's -- own contents. The buttons were never missing - they were under a 92%-opaque -- label, which is exactly what "faded and unclickable" looks like. So: backdrop -- first, contents next, chrome last, every time. function Panel:raise() local h = self.holder if not h then return end
local function up(o) if type(o) == "table" and type(o.name) == "string" then pcall(raiseWindow, o.name) end end
up(h.adjLabel) -- backdrop + title, bottom of our stack
local seen = {} local function contents(o, depth) if type(o) ~= "table" or depth > 4 or seen[o] then return end seen[o] = true up(o) if type(o.windowList) == "table" then for _, child in pairs(o.windowList) do contents(child, depth + 1) end end end contents(h.Inside, 0) contents(self.console, 0)
-- minimise/close have to stay clickable above everything we just raised up(h.minimizeLabel) up(h.exitLabel) end
function Panel:cecho(s) if self.console then aardkit.util.outw(self.console.name, s) end end
function Panel:echo(s) if self.console then self.console:echo(s) end end
function Panel:clear() if self.console then self.console:clear() end end
-- copy the line the current trigger fired on, colours intact function Panel:capture_line() if not self.console then return end selectCurrentLine() copy() appendBuffer(self.console.name) end
--- -- registry ---
function P.new(spec) assert(spec and spec.name, "panel needs a name")
local p = setmetatable({}, Panel) p.name = spec.name p.title = spec.title or spec.name p.x = spec.x or "10px" p.y = spec.y or "40px" p.w = spec.width or 460 p.h = spec.height or 220 p.fontSize = spec.fontSize p.wrap = spec.wrap p.consoleless = spec.consoleless p.onbuild = spec.onbuild p.defmode = spec.mode or DEFAULT_MODE
p:_build() if st(p.name).hidden then p.holder:hide() end
P.reg[p.name] = p return p end
-- everything of ours, above everything of theirs function P.raiseall() for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p:visible() then p:raise() end end end
function P.get(name) return P.reg[(name or ""):lower()] end
--- -- commands ---
local function list() local rows = {} for name, p in pairs(P.reg) do rows[#rows + 1] = { name, p.mode .. (p:visible() and "" or ", hidden") } end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) if #rows == 0 then U.note("No panels registered.") return end U.help("Panels", rows) end
function P.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg)
if verb == "" or verb == "list" then list()
elseif verb == "raise" or verb == "top" then P.raiseall() U.ok("Panels raised above the module's windows.")
elseif verb == "save" then if Adjustable and Adjustable.Container and Adjustable.Container.saveAll then Adjustable.Container.saveAll() end save_state() U.ok("Panel layout saved.")
elseif verb == "load" then if Adjustable and Adjustable.Container and Adjustable.Container.loadAll then Adjustable.Container.loadAll() end U.ok("Panel layout reloaded.")
elseif verb == "reset" then P.state = {} save_state() U.warn("Panel state cleared - reload the profile to rebuild them.")
elseif verb == "help" or verb == "?" then U.help("panel", { { "panel", "list every panel, its mode and visibility" }, { "panel <name> show", "show it" }, { "panel <name> hide", "hide it" }, { "panel <name> dock", "make it a real dockable window" }, { "panel <name> embed", "put it back inside the main window" }, { "panel <name> clear", "empty its buffer" }, { "panel raise", "bring every panel above the module's GUI" }, { "panel save", "write the current layout to disk" }, { "panel load", "reload the saved layout" }, { "panel reset", "forget all panel state" }, { "" }, { "Embedded panels: drag the title bar to move, edges to resize," }, { "right-click for the built-in menu. Docked panels are dragged" }, { "out to float and back onto an edge to dock; Mudlet keeps that." }, })
else local p = P.get(verb) if not p then U.warn("No panel called '" .. verb .. "'. Try 'panel' for the list.") return end local act = U.trim(rest):lower() if act == "" or act == "toggle" then p:toggle() elseif act == "show" then p:show() elseif act == "hide" then p:hide() elseif act == "dock" then p:setmode("dock") elseif act == "embed" then p:setmode("embed") elseif act == "clear" then p:clear() else U.warn("panel " .. verb .. " show|hide|dock|embed|clear") end end end
--- -- lifecycle ---
load_state()
-- Mudlet saves UserWindow geometry itself; this covers the embedded ones -- and our mode/visibility bookkeeping. function aardkit.panel.on_exit() if Adjustable and Adjustable.Container and Adjustable.Container.saveAll then pcall(Adjustable.Container.saveAll) end -- drop state for panels nothing registers any more, so retiring a plugin -- doesn't leave its geometry behind forever for name in pairs(P.state) do if not P.reg[name] then P.state[name] = nil end end save_state() end
U.killhandler(aardkit_panel_exit_handler) aardkit_panel_exit_handler = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysExitEvent", "aardkit.panel.on_exit")
-- The AardwolfMudlet GUI assembles itself on a timer after load and lands on -- top of us — that's how a panel ends up buried under the chat tabs. Raising -- once at script time is too early, so do it again once it has settled. function aardkit.panel.on_connect() -- the module's GUI assembles on its own timers and can land on top after -- any one of ours, so try at several points rather than guessing one for _, t in ipairs({ 3, 8, 15, 30 }) do tempTimer(t, P.raiseall) end end
U.killhandler(aardkit_panel_connect_handler) aardkit_panel_connect_handler = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", "aardkit.panel.on_connect")

Script.name: 20_cmd
30_tags
Script.script:
--[[ Tag gag Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
'tags on' is what makes everything else here possible — it's how the MUD tells us a spell landed, who's in the room, what's in a shop. It also dumps protocol noise all over the screen.
So: hide the tags, keep the game. Gagging in Mudlet is deleteLine(), which removes the line from the display but not from trigger processing — every plugin still sees the tag it cares about, you just stop looking at it.
Three behaviours, because tags aren't all the same shape:
line a tag that IS the payload {affon}72,1650 -> hide it block a bulk dump between markers {spellheaders}... -> hide all of it marker a wrapper round normal output {roomchars}... -> hide the markers only; the lines between are the room description you actually want to read
Unknown tags default to 'marker' — hide the wrapper, never swallow content. Guessing wrong that way costs you a stray brace; the other way costs you the game text. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.tags = aardkit.tags or {}
local T = aardkit.tags local U = aardkit.util
-- the payload IS the tag; nothing to keep local LINE = { affon = true, affoff = true, sfail = true, recon = true, recoff = true, skillgain = true, invitem = true, invmon = true, stat = true, statmon = true, chan = true, tell = true, quest = true, mapstart = true, mapend = true, }
-- Bulk dumps; hide the lot. local BLOCK = { invdata = true, skills = true, }
-- Blocks another plugin parses. We keep our hands entirely off these — not the -- contents, not even the markers. -- -- Removing them from BLOCK wasn't enough: the marker triggers below are generic -- and were still deleting the {/tag} line before the parser could see it, so its -- capture never closed. And the rows got deleteLine()'d twice, which is what -- left blank gaps in the output. One owner per block, all the way through. local OWNED = { spellheaders = true, recoveries = true, coords = true, }
-- wrappers around text worth reading; hide only the markers local MARKER = { roomchars = true, rdesc = true, exits = true, roomname = true, }
local CFG = U.load("tags", { on = true, extra = {} })
-- anything the user adds by hand for name, how in pairs(CFG.extra or {}) do if how == "line" then LINE[name] = true elseif how == "block" then BLOCK[name] = true else MARKER[name] = true end end
local inblock, block_trig, block_timer = nil, nil, nil
local function kind(name) if LINE[name] then return "line" end if BLOCK[name] then return "block" end return "marker" end
-- A block's contents aren't tagged, so swallowing them needs a catch-all — and a -- PERMANENT catch-all would run Lua on every line the MUD ever sends. Arm one -- only for the length of the block instead, the way Who Poller does its gag. local function close_block() inblock = nil if block_trig then killTrigger(block_trig); block_trig = nil end if block_timer then killTimer(block_timer); block_timer = nil end end
local function open_block(name) close_block() inblock = name block_trig = tempRegexTrigger("^.*$", function() deleteLine() end) -- if the closing marker never lands, let go rather than eating the session block_timer = tempTimer(6, function() if inblock then close_block() U.warn("Tag gag: {" .. tostring(name) .. "} never closed, released.") end end) end
--- -- triggers ---
-- an opening marker or a self-contained tag: ^{name}rest function T.on_open(name) if not CFG.on then return end name = (name or ""):lower() if OWNED[name] then return end -- its parser gags it deleteLine() if kind(name) == "block" then open_block(name) end -- 'line' and 'marker' both just lose this one line end
-- a closing marker: ^{/name} function T.on_close(name) if not CFG.on then return end if OWNED[(name or ""):lower()] then return end deleteLine() if inblock and (name or ""):lower() == inblock then close_block() end end
--- -- commands ---
local function listing() local function names(t) local a = {} for k in pairs(t) do a[#a + 1] = k end table.sort(a) return table.concat(a, " ") end U.help("Tag gag", { { "gagging", CFG.on and "on" or "OFF" }, { "" }, { "line (hidden entirely)" }, { " " .. names(LINE) }, { "block (hidden with their contents)" }, { " " .. names(BLOCK) }, { "marker (markers hidden, text kept)" }, { " " .. names(MARKER) }, { "owned (left alone; another plugin parses them)" }, { " " .. names(OWNED) }, { "" }, { "aardtags off", "show the raw tags again" }, { "aardtags line|block|marker <tag>", "classify one yourself" }, { "aardtags forget <tag>", "drop a custom classification" }, { "" }, { "Gagging hides lines from the screen only - every plugin still" }, { "sees them, so nothing stops working." }, }) end
function T.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest):lower()
if verb == "" or verb == "list" or verb == "status" then listing()
elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then CFG.on = (verb == "on") close_block() U.save("tags", CFG) U.ok("Tag gag " .. verb .. ".")
elseif verb == "line" or verb == "block" or verb == "marker" then if rest == "" then U.warn("Usage: aardtags " .. verb .. " <tagname>") return end LINE[rest], BLOCK[rest], MARKER[rest] = nil, nil, nil if verb == "line" then LINE[rest] = true elseif verb == "block" then BLOCK[rest] = true else MARKER[rest] = true end CFG.extra[rest] = verb U.save("tags", CFG) U.ok("{" .. rest .. "} treated as " .. verb .. ".")
elseif verb == "forget" then if CFG.extra[rest] then CFG.extra[rest] = nil U.save("tags", CFG) U.ok("{" .. rest .. "} back to its default; reload to apply.") else U.warn("No custom rule for {" .. rest .. "}.") end
else listing() end end
aardkit.register("tags", "hide Aardwolf's protocol tags from the screen", T.cmd)

Script.name: 40_stock
Script.script:
--[==[ Standing clear of the stock AardwolfMudlet module Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
A short list of things in aardwolf.xml that actively misbehave, switched off so they stop interfering. Nothing here edits their package - we only disable by name at runtime, so their file is untouched and a reinstall or update of theirs just gets disabled again next load.
Currently one entry, 'runto rt':
elseif string.match("the witches of omen tor omentor", matches[2]:lower()) send("run 2s10e2n7e7n11e4n4e;enter hole") --vidblain tempTimer(1,[[aard.coordrun(15578)]])
It swallows every 'runto' and answers a handful of them with speedwalks hardcoded to whoever wrote it, so 'runto omentor' sends someone else's Vidblain route and the MUD answers "Invalid directions in command."
Then it calls aard.coordrun, which is worse:
function aard.coordrun(roomid) if aard.state == 3 and ...areaName... == "vidblain" then display(aard.state) ; gotoRoom(roomid) else display(aard.state) aard.crun = tempTimer(1, function () aard.coordrun(roomid) end) end end
Anywhere but Vidblain that's an infinite loop printing aard.state - a bare "3" every second, forever, with a fresh timer per 'runto' you type. Only the newest is tracked in aard.crun, so the rest run until you reconnect.
Disabling their alias hands 'runto' back to the MUD, which is what it should have been doing. ]==]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.stock = aardkit.stock or {}
local S = aardkit.stock local U = aardkit.util
local CFG = U.load("stock", { off = { ["runto rt"] = true } })
-- why each one is switched off, shown by 'aardkit stock' local WHY = { ["runto rt"] = "hardcodes someone else's speedwalks and leaks a 1/sec timer printing '3'", }
function S.apply() local n = 0 for name, want in pairs(CFG.off) do if want then local ok = pcall(disableAlias, name) if ok then n = n + 1 end end end -- their runaway timer, if one is already going. Only the newest is tracked -- on their side, so anything older survives until you reconnect. if aard and aard.crun then pcall(killTimer, aard.crun) aard.crun = nil end return n end
function S.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest)
if verb == "" or verb == "list" then local rows = {} for name, want in pairs(CFG.off) do rows[#rows + 1] = { name, (want and "disabled" or "left alone") .. (WHY[name] and (" - " .. WHY[name]) or "") } end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock on <alias>", "let the module's alias run again" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock off <alias>", "switch it off again" } U.help("Stock module", rows)
elseif verb == "on" and rest ~= "" then CFG.off[rest] = nil U.save("stock", CFG) pcall(enableAlias, rest) U.ok("Left '" .. rest .. "' alone. Reload to be sure it's back.")
elseif verb == "off" and rest ~= "" then CFG.off[rest] = true U.save("stock", CFG) pcall(disableAlias, rest) U.ok("Disabled '" .. rest .. "'.")
else U.warn("aardkit stock [list | on <alias> | off <alias>]") end end
-- Their package loads on its own schedule, so once at script time isn't enough: -- an alias they create after us would come back up enabled. S.apply() tempTimer(2, S.apply)
U.killhandler(aardkit_stock_connect) aardkit_stock_connect = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", function() tempTimer(3, S.apply) end)
